To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
local cytoreduction of the primary tumorous lesion and/or metastases thereof is associated with survival benefits in patients with metastasized prostate cancer.

local cytoreductive therapy of the prostate cancer primary tumour (and/or metastatic disease) in men with de-novo metastatic prostate cancer can provide additional survival benefits when combined with systemic therapy.

cytoreductive treatment strategies, including metastasis directed therapy, are increasingly used in men with de nov metastatic prostate cancer and that these strategies can provide substantial survival benefits.

the development of novel treatment modalities in prostate cancer, with the aim of improving the outcomes for patients with this common disease.

the current evidence base supports the use of cytoreductive treatment strategies (with radiotherapy and/or ablative therapies) as part of the management of de novo metastatic (oligo- or poly-) prostate cancer in combination with systemic treatment.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cytoreduction of the primary prostate cancer and/or metastases is an important component of treatment for patients in this population.

local treatment of the primary prostate cancer (or metastases thereof), in combination with systemic therapies, can provide a survival benefit in men with de nuevo, synchronous castration sensitive, metastatic prostate cancer.

cytoreductive treatment strategies are a promising treatment approach for men with de novo metastases, and further randomized controlled trials are urgently required to confirm the survival benefits that have already been observed in this patient population.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cytoreduction is a viable treatment option for patients with oligometastatic disease.
the use of local cytoreductive therapies, such as prostatectomy or radiotherapy, in men with oligometastatic disease should be further explored.
cytoreductive treatment strategies can be used to delay disease progression and improve outcomes in patients with de novo oligorecurrent prostate cancer.
